newsitem.title: USA: Chiron, Green Cross expand HIV drug tests.
newsitem.headline: Chiron, Green Cross expand HIV drug tests.

text.p: Chiron Corp on Wednesday said it and Green Cross Corp have agreed to expand human clinical studies of their immunotherapeutic HIV-IT(V).

Green Cross, based in Osaka, Japan, will provide an additional $4 million this year to conduct Phase II trials that use HIV-IT(V) in combination with anti-retroviral protease inhibitors. The tests will be conducted in about 200 HIV-positive patients, Chiron said.
HIV-IT(V) is a non-replicating retroviral vector that delivers the genes encoding the HIV env and rev proteins.
The product is administered through intramuscular injection. Preclinical and Phase 1 studies have indicated that the drug induces killer T-cells against HIV-infected cells.
A Phase II trial for HIV-IT(V), begun in December 1994, is currently underway about 200 patients.
Under the terms of the collaboration with Green Cross, Chiron performs research, development, and manufacturing for HIV-IT(V), and Green Cross retains worldwide marketing rights.
